ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against: (1) the New Zealand Police financial intelligence and Companies Office disqualification registers; (2) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (3) the United Nations Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List; (4) the New Zealand Consolidated Sanctions List administered under the Sanctions Act 2022; and (5) PEP datasets covering prominent public functions, immediate family and close associates. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP or negative match; screening must be repeated at incorporation, on each new UBO appointment, and annually thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Name Reservation and Company Registration portal at https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English/Latin script; te reo Māori words are permitted and macrons are accepted. Non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into an English or Māori form. A name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name, must not be offensive or misleading, and must include 'Limited' (or 'Tapui Limited') where limited liability protection is sought. Any restricted or sensitive word requires prior approval from the relevant regulatory agency.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the agent receives the Registrar's written reasons in the Companies Office portal. The applicant may file an administrative appeal within 20 working days by selecting the original reservation reference and submitting submissions addressing the identical/confusing similarity findings or attaching a consent letter from the relevant regulator for a restricted token; the Registrar will review within 15 working days. If the appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may apply to the High Court of New Zealand for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016. Only a fresh reservation may be made after the validity period lapses, except that before expiry the applicant may apply for an extension if incorporation is pending and supported by a satisfactory explanation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is legally permissible as a registered office under section 87 of the Companies Act 1993, provided it is a physical street address in New Zealand, not a post office box, and mail and service of process are effectively received and forwarded. For a TikTok MCN agency, a virtual office may be accepted initially but will increase AML/CFT and substance scrutiny if the company obtains Wise B2B or TikTok Creator Payout payment rails, because banks and payment intermediaries require physical business address, beneficial ownership disclosure and evidence of genuine commercial activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but quantifiable: approximately 5-10% in the first 12 months for a standard low-risk MCN company with proper registered office agreements; the risk rises to 25-30% where virtual-only office is used, high cross-border creator payments are processed, or a UBO fails to provide bank-referenced source-of-funds documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act No. 105 of 1993), sections 10 (Limited Liability), 12–19 (Incorporation Procedure), 20 (Constitution), 21 (Company Name), 46 (Registered Office), 47 (Delivery of Address for Service), 98–100 (Share Capital and Minimum Capital), 108 (Charges), 151 (Consent to Appointment of Director), 200–210 (Annual Returns); Financial Reporting Act 2013; Income Tax Act 2007 section YC 2 (Non-Resident Company Taxation)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZ1 — Application for Incorporation of a Company Limited by Shares (filed electronically through the Companies Office E-Registration Portal, RealMe authenticated)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Section 98(1)(a) of the Companies Act 1993 imposes no minimum paid-up capital threshold; shares may be issued at nominal par value and remain partly paid or unpaid. No escrow account, capital deposit, or capital import certificate is required. The Company must issue at least one share and maintain at least one class of shares. Non-resident ownership is permitted without any capital contribution restriction.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (THE "COMPANY") UNANIMOUSLY PASSED ON [DATE] IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. RESOLVED THAT: 1. INCORPORATION: The application for incorporation filed with the New Zealand Companies Office (Form NZ1) and the accompanying Constitution are hereby approved, ratified, and confirmed. 2. INITIAL SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION: The Company shall issue, and the subscriber shareholders, all being non-resident of New Zealand, shall subscribe for, the initial issued share capital of the Company, being [NUMBER] ordinary shares of NZD $0.10 each, fully paid at par value. The Board notes that the Companies Act 1993 does not require any minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company shall be situated and maintained at [ADDRESS OF NEW ZEALAND REGISTERED OFFICE] in accordance with section 46 of the Companies Act 1993, and the delivery address for service of documents shall be [●]. 4. DIRECTOR AND OFFICERS: [●] (full name and address) is hereby appointed as a Director of the Company to hold office in accordance with section 151 of the Companies Act 1993, and [●] is hereby appointed as Company Secretary (where applicable). Each appointed director shall execute a formal Consent to Appointment (Form NZ2). 5. NON-RESIDENT TAX TREATMENT: The Board records that the Company shall be managed and controlled outside New Zealand and shall claim treatment as a non-resident company for income tax purposes under section YC 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007, such that no New Zealand income tax liability arises absent New Zealand-sourced income. 6. BANK ACCOUNT AND CORPORATE SEAL: The Board authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts, the adoption of a common seal, and the execution of any documents necessary to give effect to the foregoing. RESOLVED FURTHER that the Director be authorized to complete, execute, and deliver all documents, filings, and applications ancillary to the incorporation and initial administration of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Optional Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Company Name Register (online search portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and does not breach the Name Approval Guidelines under section 22(3) of the Companies Act 1993. For an international non-resident company, the corporate name must ordinarily end with 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation. If the name is to be protected pending the incorporation filing, reserve the name for up to 20 working days; otherwise, proceed directly to incorporation filing on the same day.
required_dossiers: Statement of entity purpose and business scope (ISIC 7310 — Advertising and Creator MCN Agency)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar declines the name, the applicant may file a fresh application with an alternative name or seek reconsideration through the Companies Office Name Application Enquiry channel; a written refusal may be appealed to the Registrar under section 22(3) of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution and Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution in accordance with section 20 of the Companies Act 1993, ensuring no provision contracts out of the applied provisions listed in Schedule 1 of the Act. Prepare the Shareholders' Subscription Agreement, the Director's Consent (Form NZ2), and the Registered Office Agency Agreement. For the single-shareholder international holding structure, record the ultimate beneficial ownership and the intended non-resident tax treatment in the internal governance register without filing beneficial ownership details publicly.
required_dossiers: Form NZ2 — Consent to Appointment of Director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries any constitutional clause as impermissible under section 20(2) of the Companies Act 1993, the Board must pass a special resolution to amend the constitution and resubmit the corrected copy before the incorporation application is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Form NZ1 Incorporation Application and Payment of Registration Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — E-Registration Portal (RealMe authenticated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Office E-Registration Portal using RealMe, complete Form NZ1 (Application for Incorporation of a Company Limited by Shares), record the registered office address (a physical address in New Zealand), the address for service, the directors' and shareholders' details, the share structure, and the optional constitution. Attach the executed Form NZ2 and the constitution, certify compliance with the Companies Act 1993, and pay the prescribed registration fee online by credit or debit card.
required_dossiers: Form NZ2 — Consent to Appointment of Director
Registered office address and address for service details
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is placed under query, the applicant must respond through the portal within 10 working days; unresolved queries result in withdrawal of the application, with the filing fee refunded or re-applied upon resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Inland Revenue Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (issuance) / Inland Revenue (IRD number enrolment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation together with a 9-digit company registration number. The Companies Office automatically notifies Inland Revenue, which issues the company's IRD number for income tax purposes. If the international company intends to remain non-resident for tax, the Board must ensure that no New Zealand-sourced income is derived and must file a non-residence declaration with its tax advisors; GST registration is optional where no taxable supply is expected in New Zealand.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is not auto-issued within 5 business days, the Company should file Form IRD 596 (Request for IRD Number) with Inland Revenue; if the Certificate of Incorporation is defective, the Company may apply at the Companies Office for a certified copy of the certificate under section 213 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Activation of Registered Office, Corporate Registers and Annual Return Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the statutory registers required by the Companies Act 1993: the share register, register of directors, register of charges, and accounting records. Appoint the New Zealand registered agent where the company is administered by a registered office provider, confirm that the registered office physically displays the company name, and set a calendar reminder for the annual return, which must be filed every year with the Companies Office within 30 days of the anniversary of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to file the annual return on time triggers a default notice from the Companies Office; the remedy is to file the annual return within 30 days of the due date and pay the late filing fee to avoid removal from the register.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial authority licensure is required for the creator agency (ISIC 7310 Advertising) activity; the only relevant administrative body is the local Territorial Authority (e.g., Auckland Council) acting as Building Consent Authority for premises compliance under the Building Act 2004.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no operating or manufacturing permit is mandated. A TikTok Multi-Channel Network (MCN) agency and advertising services company (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810) is a permitted administrative activity. The Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 is not engaged absent the provision of financial services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) and the relevant Territorial Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Exempt — Not required. The proposed activity is an administrative office and digital services operation (creator incubation and talent representation) that does not appear in the Fourth Schedule of the Resource Management Act 1991; no full Environmental Impact Assessment report or Assessment of Environmental Effects is legally mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — the operation produces zero industrial wastewater and zero VOC or point-source emissions. General office waste must comply with the Territorial Authority Waste Management Plan and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; any disposal of electronic equipment must follow Ministry for the Environment e-waste (WEEE) guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety: a Form FSA — Fire Safety compliance certificate is required for the commercial office premises under the Building Act 2004, issued by the local Building Consent Authority. Electrical Certification: an 'ES1 Certificate of Electrical Work' is required for any new or altered electrical installations under the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010. Occupational Clearance: the workplace must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a documented worker engagement protocol and a Job Safety Analysis for any content production or studio space. Structural load inspection is not required for standard office fit-out unless the premises accommodate studio hardware or set equipment that alters slab loading, in which case Building Consent works must be obtained under the Building Act 2004.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue / Te Tari Taake), New Zealand; official online portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz). Export and customs matters are administered by the New Zealand Customs Service (Te Mana Ārai o Aotearoa) under the Customs and Excise Act 2018.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign entity with a New Zealand tax nexus (carrying on a taxable activity, deriving New Zealand-source income, or required to register for GST) must apply to Inland Revenue for an IRD number by completing form IR742 (Non-Resident Tax Registration) or by registering through myIR where an NZ bank account and registered address are held; the entity must first be validly incorporated or registered as an overseas company on the New Zealand Companies Register and provide certified foreign registration documents, director and resident agent details, and the principal business address; GST registration is then filed separately in myIR using the GST registration application (GSTREG), which issues a GST number linked to the same IRD number; a non-resident may register for GST voluntarily when making taxable supplies, and registration takes effect from the date the taxable activity commences or the date approved by the Commissioner.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone - Non-resident International Company (IC) incorporated as a tax-exempt offshore vehicle under Cook Islands international company legislation, as recognised under New Zealand's territorial scope; the entity is treated as having no New Zealand income tax nexus unless it establishes a fixed place of business or permanent establishment in New Zealand; global TikTok creator agency income (creator incubation, multi-channel talent representation, and brand-facilitation commissions) sourced and consummated outside New Zealand is exempt from New Zealand income tax, and New Zealand GST applies only to supplies connected with New Zealand consumption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; the principal statutory elections are: ordinary company vs Look-Through Company (LTC) status under subpart HA of the Income Tax Act 2007 (with the five-owner and eligibility tests), the CFC attributable CFC income election and active income de minimis exemption under subparts CQ and EX of the Income Tax Act 2007, the GST registration threshold election, the foreign currency accounting elections, and the hybrid mismatch rules in Part FA of the Income Tax Act 2007 which operate to disallow deduction/non-inclusion mismatches and imported mismatches for cross-border structured arrangements involving offshore entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax) - a value-added tax system administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies (excluding GST) in any 12-month period in New Zealand; a non-resident carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand must register once this economic turnover threshold is exceeded and may voluntarily register under section 51 of the GST Act 1985 before reaching the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, API transmission, or digital stamping regime exists in New Zealand; B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and interoperable via the Peppol network; GST invoices may be issued electronically provided they satisfy the content requirements in section 24 of the GST Act 1985; export declarations and supporting export data must instead be lodged electronically with the New Zealand Customs Service via the Trade Single Window (TSW), using an approved software system, before goods depart New Zealand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under sections 11 and 11A of the GST Act 1985: (1) goods physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier or an agent within 28 days of the time of supply (or such extended period as the Commissioner approves); and (2) services supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, where the supply is not made to a New Zealand GST-registered recipient for use in a New Zealand taxable activity and is not connected with land or movable property in New Zealand. For a global TikTok MCN agency, creator incubation, talent management, performance tracking, and brand-negotiation services rendered for the benefit of non-resident creators and offshore advertisers qualify as zero-rated offshore services when the contract, service delivery, and consumption all occur outside New Zealand; the supplier must retain adequate documentary evidence proving the offshore character of each supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Combined Export Declaration / Export Entry lodged electronically with the New Zealand Customs Service through the Trade Single Window prior to departure)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (transport document evidencing physical export of goods from New Zealand and overseas destination)

Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign exchange settlement statement (bank statement or Wise B2B payout statement evidencing receipt of cross-border settlement in a New Zealand or foreign bank account and the corresponding foreign exchange conversion)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner of Inland Revenue may audit export zero-rating claims retrospectively and, where a zero-rating condition is not substantiated, re-characterise the supply as standard-rated GST at 15%, with use-of-money interest running from the original return date; shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 escalate by culpability: 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness or a hidden arrangement, and 100% to 150% for evasion or an abusive tax position; knowingly lodging false export declarations or fabricating inward remittance evidence may result in criminal prosecution, imprisonment, and full GST clawback extending the assessment period to 7 years (no time limit in cases of fraud or evasion).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), operating as the prudential regulator and apex clearing-system supervisor under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021; foreign-exchange control functions are no longer exercised through a separate exchange-control authority, and transaction-level FX governance is discharged by the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand holds IMF Article VIII status; both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible with no residual exchange controls, no central-bank licensing of foreign-exchange payments, and no restrictions on dividend, interest, royalty, or capital repatriation. Practical remittance hurdles are limited to AML/CFT-driven source-of-funds verification, FATCA/CRS self-certification, and, for the CK_IC vehicle, production of a New Zealand-certified non-resident status opinion so that the bank does not erroneously apply NRWT or classify the entity as a New Zealand tax resident. The tax-exempt International Company may hold multi-currency accounts, convert NZD on demand, and repatriate profits without prior regulatory consent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender rules exist in New Zealand. The statutory framework (Exchange Control Act 1978 having been repealed, and no successor regime being enacted) imposes no mandatory conversion ratio, no prescribed settlement timeline, and no requirement to confide export proceeds to the Reserve Bank. A creator-incubation agency may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts in offshore or onshore foreign-currency accounts, may invoice and settle in USD, EUR, CNH, or NZD, and may apply those receipts directly to overseas creator-payout obligations. The only obligation is correct balance-of-payments reporting by the receiving bank and ordinary tax documentation where the income is assessable in New Zealand.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Multi-Currency Account
Core NZD Operational Account / International Transaction Account
Operational Account with Dedicated FX Forward Booking
Escrow and Clearing Account with Trade Desk Integration
Domestic Settlement Account / Secondary Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for disbursement execution but only Medium as a primary settlement house. Wise (Wise B2B, formerly TransferWise) is the designated payout rail for TikTok creator settlements and is registered as a New Zealand Financial Service Provider (FSP) and a reporting entity under the AML/CFT Act; it may hold NZD balances indirectly through partner banks (including Westpac) but is not a licensed registered bank in New Zealand. Airwallex and Payoneer offer similar B2B payout capabilities; nevertheless, the CK_IC treasury policy must be: (i) the Tier-1 New Zealand bank remains the sole concentration and escrow layer, (ii) Wise B2B serves strictly as creator-payout distribution rail, and (iii) no offshore EMI may open or maintain the capital escrow account or receive platform settlement without passing through the NZ-regulated clearing chain. Legal constraint: any non-NZ EMI that operates without FSP registration cannot lawfully provide payment services to New Zealand-based treasury functions and would jeopardize the entity's bank relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the CK_IC (a non-resident, tax-exempt International Company), all Tier-1 New Zealand banks mandate at least one natural-person director or ultimate beneficial owner to attend an in-person or bank-approved video interview, accompanied by a notarized corporate KYC dossier; a fully remote, no-appearance account opening is not currently available for offshore corporate entities. In practice, the bank will also require physical verification of a New Zealand-resident designated signatory or licensed agent (barrister/solicitor or chartered accountant) who endorses the company's constitutional documents and beneficial-ownership declarations. Directors resident in Asia-Pacific time zones may complete the interview via the international banking desk (teleconference plus scanned certified copies) provided originals are couriered to the branch before the account is activated; non-certified electronic copies alone will be rejected.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company status — the bank perceives the CK_IC as a zero-tax, tax-haven-flagged structure requiring enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal New Zealand tax residence opinion from a licensed chartered accountant, OECD CRS-FATCA self-certification (Form W-8BEN-E where applicable), an economic-substance memorandum evidencing real creator-management activity, and a certified Board resolution declaring the absence of New Zealand-source operational income.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the beneficial-ownership chain, including nominee shareholders, a Cook Islands trustee, or a discretionary trust standing behind the MCN treasury structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership and control chart to ultimate natural persons, registered-agent certificate from the incorporating registry, trust deed (where relevant), certified passports and address proofs of all ultimate beneficial owners, and a sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statement, each notarized or covered by a licensed New Zealand lawyer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value creator disbursements that the bank may characterize as laundered value movement or unlicensed money-service business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed creator onboarding contracts, TikTok Creator Payout settlement statements showing platform-verified deductions, a client-vendor registry mapping each disbursement to a verified creator, and a monthly reconciliation of the Wise B2B ledger against the Tier-1 bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments to creators could be recharacterized as employment or withholding-taxable New Zealand remuneration, triggering NRWT and payroll compliance flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent contractor classification memorandum, tax residence certificates of each payee creator, IRD non-resident withholding tax exemption or certificate where available, and the MCN's statutory declaration that all creators are engaged as independent talent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained FX forward and spot turnover arising from USD/NZD conversion of TikTok revenue, which may be viewed as speculative dealing inconsistent with the low-risk standard tier.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury and FX policy, cash-flow forecast with creator payout commitments, a copy of the ISDA or FX mandate with the Tier-1 bank, daily treasury worksheet demonstrating natural hedging limits, and monthly bank covenant compliance reporting.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital should be injected as equity (preferred) via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's account to the CK_IC's NZD capital escrow account at ANZ, BNZ, or Westpac, referencing 'INVCAP / SHARE CAPITAL CK_IC' and the Companies Office shareholder resolution as remittance instruction; the New Zealand receiving bank will code the receipt as non-resident inward direct investment for balance-of-payments reporting and will release funds only after the corporate KYC pack, share register, and trust-deed disclosure have been verified. No Overseas Investment Act 2005 consent is triggered for a non-sensitive creator-agency business, and no Reserve Bank approval is required. If the injection is instead structured as a shareholder loan, a valid loan agreement, arm's-length interest rate, and thin-capitalization documentation must accompany the wire, otherwise the bank may re-book the credit as paid-in capital and the Inland Revenue Department may recharacterize deductibility. TikTok platform-generated revenue should not be routed as a capital injection; it should flow from TikTok (USD) to Wise B2B, then be converted through the Tier-1 bank's FX desk into NZD only when treasury requires liquidity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Creator settlements and agency disbursements should clear through SWIFT MT103 FFC transfers from the CK_IC's Tier-1 NZD operational account using payment purpose code 'Management Fees / Talent Management Commission', with the beneficiary bank's SWIFT BIC and the creator's tax identifier embedded in the reference field. For high-value regional co-commission arrangements, a Commercial Letter of Credit (usance or sight) or Bank Payment Obligation (BPO) may be issued where TikTok's regional procurement desk requires documentary settlement; each LC must be issued on the entity's board-approved facility with full compliance with UCP600. The TikTok Creator Payout rail aggregates micro-disbursements in USD and converts through Wise B2B, leveraging local-clearing rails (SEPA, Fedwire/ACH, Faster Payments) for last-mile distribution, thereby preserving the NZD operating account as a concentration point rather than a high-velocity transaction trap. All outbound instructions must be dual-approved and mirror the approved creator registry.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD outright forwards and rolling forward contracts booked with Tier-1 RBNZ-supervised banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or thin-liquidity creator-market currencies (USD/CNH, USD/IDR, USD/PHP, USD/THB) where local deliverability constraints apply
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR) to hedge capital-injection balances and profit-repatriation exposures
FX swap and tom-next roll transactions used to manage daily treasury liquidity mismatches between TikTok USD receipts and NZD disbursements
Plain-vanilla EUR/USD and USD/NZD European-style FX options providing downside protection on the platform revenue pipeline without speculative intent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Licence Fee and Annual Return (Form AR) for International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Cook Islands Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation date each year; registered agent issues renewal invoice 30 days pre-due date; no statutory grace period for payment of the prescribed government fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee (minimum NZ$100) plus compounding penalty for each additional month of default; after 6 months of continued non-payment the Registrar issues a notice of proposed strike-off, and upon expiry without remedy the company is dissolved and struck off with assets forfeited to the Crown.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Trust Company acting as registered agent (maintaining the FSRA-approved agency record)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; the registered agent service agreement and office consent must be renewed prior to each anniversary and maintained continuously thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the registered agent resigns and no replacement licensed agent is appointed within the statutory replacement period (typically 30 days), the Registrar may suspend the company, initiate strike-off, and the directors may be disqualified for failure to maintain a registered agent and office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation and Shareholding Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent / Financial Intelligence Unit (confidential UBO register; no public filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the anniversary of incorporation and within 14 days of any transfer or allotment of shares or any change in ultimate beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporate fine of up to NZ$50,000 and continuing daily default fines for failure to provide accurate UBO updates; the registered agent may refuse to process annual renewal, and sustained non-compliance triggers administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Registers Maintenance and Board Minute Records (on-site inspection readiness)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Office (available for inspection by the Registrar and authorised officers on demand)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; every change in directors, members, or charges must be recorded in the statutory registers within 10 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of up to NZ$10,000 against the company and each defaulting director; deliberate destruction or falsification of registers may result in personal liability, director disqualification, and strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a standard Cook Islands International Company that is not licensed under the Banks Act 2003, Insurance Act 2005, or Financial Services Act; the low-risk MCN/creator-agency scope (ISIC 7310) falls outside the compulsory audit net. An audit or accountant's report becomes mandatory only if the FSRA directed such review or the entity engages in regulated financial business.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The directors must maintain accounting records sufficient to explain transactions and enable true and fair financial statements to be prepared; no financial statements are filed with the Registrar for tax-exempt International Companies, but where prepared, the board adopts IFRS / NZ IFRS-equivalent as the applicable framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must keep a confidential beneficial ownership register at its registered office and deliver an updated UBO schedule to its licensed registered agent annually on the anniversary of incorporation, as well as within 14 days of any share transfer, allotment, or change in ultimate beneficial ownership. The agent submits the prescribed UBO data to the Cook Islands Financial Intelligence Unit / Registrar; the register is not open to public inspection. Failure to provide accurate confirmation may invalidate the annual renewal and trigger strike-off.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 – US$2,500 per year (licensed Cook Islands registered agent inclusive of registered office, annual return preparation, and confidential UBO filing)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500 – US$8,000 per engagement (not mandatory; incurred only if a shareholder, investor, or financial institution requires a certified audit)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective New Zealand tax rate for the CK_IC International Company in the Tax-Exempt Zone classification: a non-resident international company deriving only foreign-sourced income and having no New Zealand fixed establishment is outside the New Zealand income tax net. For any New Zealand-resident entity conducting the MCN agency, the standard 28% corporate rate applies with no general tax holiday; available incentives include the 15% R&D Tax Credit for eligible innovation expenditure and depreciable capital allowances. The IC tax-exempt status is preserved only where management and control, creator contracts, and revenue generation remain offshore.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No fixed statutory cap; New Zealand permits indefinite carry-forward of tax losses under ITA 2007 s IA 4, subject to the shareholder continuity rules requiring 49% continuity for carrying forward losses against the same/similar business and 66% continuity for all other businesses. A continuity breach forfeits the loss balance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the Inland Revenue (IRD) myIR secure online portal or through approved tax agent gateway software. Non-resident companies with New Zealand-source taxable income must also register with IRD and obtain an IRD number before filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, aligned to the New Zealand standard tax year (1 April to 31 March). Non-standard balance dates require IRD approval. Provisional tax is payable during the year in three instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date company: IR4 return due by 7 July following year-end when filed electronically; paper returns due 7 May. Terminal tax due 7 April (or 7 July where the electronic filing/tax agent extension applies). Provisional tax instalments due 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from creator incubation, TikTok platform revenue share, MCN commission, talent agency fees, sponsorship and advertising income, and any other amounts derived from business activity, excluding GST collected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only New Zealand-sourced gross income attributable to a New Zealand fixed establishment. Offshore creator management fees and TikTok payouts received outside New Zealand are excluded from this box for a non-resident IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All interest received or accrued, including bank interest and debt instrument returns, before deduction of resident withholding tax (RWT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only interest arising from New Zealand sources, e.g., NZ bank deposits. Interest derived by a non-resident IC from offshore accounts is non-assessable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends received from New Zealand-resident companies, grossed up for imputation credits, and excluded dividends from non-resident companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign dividends are not returned by a non-resident IC unless it has a New Zealand PE and the dividends are attributable to that PE; CFC/FIF attribution rules apply only to NZ-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Miscellaneous assessable income: royalties, IP licensing fees, influencer database licensing, FX gains, government grants, and any unusual or non-trading income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties sourced in New Zealand are subject to final NRWT at source and should be excluded from the IR4 where no PE exists; if a PE exists, return the royalty net of expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Arithmetic total of Boxes 1 through 4; all assessable income derived during the income year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC claiming tax-exempt-zone status will generally show nil total income unless it carries on business through a NZ fixed establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible business expenses: creator advances written off, talent acquisition fees, staff salaries, FBT on non-cash benefits, SaaS platform fees, analytics software, advertising, legal, accounting, rent, contractor payments, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses incurred in deriving New Zealand-source assessable income are deductible. Head-office allocations, offshore management charges, and intra-group fees must satisfy the arm's-length standard under s GC 13 and thin capitalisation under s FE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before loss offset, computed as Box 5 minus Box 6, with non-deductible items (50% entertainment, fines, non-commercial payments) added back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident IC with a NZ PE, net income must be computed on the OECD Article 7 attributable-profits basis, not on worldwide accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unused tax losses from prior income years applied against current-year net income, subject to continuity certification attached in the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC may only offset losses attributable to its NZ PE and must evidence shareholder continuity; offshore holding-company changes may forfeit the loss balance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits claimed: 33% RWT withheld on NZ interest and non-imputed dividends, plus imputation credits attached to fully imputed NZ dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC cannot generally claim NZ imputation credits; distributions received from NZ companies suffer final NRWT at source. Leave this box nil unless the IC is NZ-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Residual Income Tax / Refund Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net position after credits: terminal tax payable or refund due, including use-of-money interest calculations where underpayments or overpayments exist.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A tax-exempt IC with nil NZ-source income will show zero residual tax; a nil return should still be filed to preserve compliance history and avoid the late-filing penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under TAA 1994 s 139A: NZ$250 per month or part-month for companies, capped at NZ$1,000. Late payment penalty under s 139B: 1% immediately after the due date, an additional 4% on day 8, then a further 1% per month thereafter. Use-of-money interest accrues on unpaid terminal tax at the prescribed rate (approximately 8.2% per annum). Continued non-filing exposes directors to prosecution under s 143A, with fines up to NZ$50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% NRWT on non-imputed dividends; 15% NRWT on fully imputed dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident (ITA 2007 s RF 9). A Tax-Exempt Zone IC distributing profits is not an NZ-resident payer and incurs no NZ NRWT on offshore distributions; however, if the IC elects or is deemed NZ-resident, the full imputation/NRWT architecture applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To access a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain an official Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) submit the TRC and a completed IR67 declaration or relevant IRD exemption certificate to the New Zealand payer before payment; (3) be the beneficial owner of the income and satisfy the treaty's limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose test. The NZ payer must retain the documentation to justify applying the treaty rate. Retroactive treaty claims are processed via an amended IR4 or IR67 and may attract shortfall penalties if the original withholding was unreasonable. Disputes are resolved through the applicable MAP procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT: 15% on royalties and 15% on interest paid by NZ-resident persons to non-residents. The Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) reduces interest withholding to 2% where the NZ borrower is an approved issuer and the lender is not a related non-resident. Under New Zealand's DTAs, treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 10% and royalties to 5%-10%; dividends generally to 15% (5% for corporate holders of at least 10% of the voting power). Payments to non-resident TikTok creators classified as royalties for content/IP usage are subject to 15% NRWT; payments for offshore services fall outside NRWT but may trigger the non-resident contractor schedular payment regime where services are physically performed in New Zealand.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand has no statutory Local File/Master File filing requirement, but taxpayer documentation must be prepared and produced to IRD on request. IRD risk-assessment de minimis thresholds: NZ$5,000,000 for cross-border goods transactions; NZ$1,000,000 per annum for services, intangibles, financing, and guarantee transactions. The CK_IC MCN's cross-border creator payouts, platform revenue-share arrangements, and intra-group management fees at or above these thresholds require contemporaneous OECD-aligned TP documentation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) - benchmarked against independent platform revenue-share rates and creator commission schedules
Resale Price Method - MCN agency commission structure where the IC resells platform inventory/creator slots
Cost Plus Method - creator management services priced at arm's-length cost plus an appropriate gross margin
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) - operating margin of the NZ MCN entity compared with comparable advertising and talent agency benchmarks
Profit Split Method - integrated value chain where both TikTok platform intangibles and creator/agency functions contribute significant non-routine intangibles
